summary: Build reproducible parallel sampling without reusing random streams accidentally or confusing sampling error with arithmetic error.
outcomes: Assign random sequences to logical samples reproducibly.
Report Monte Carlo uncertainty separately from runtime and numerical error.
sequence: Generate and inspect a tiny seeded sample stream.
Map sample identifiers to parallel generators or counters.
Expose repeated seeds and state-reuse mistakes.
Estimate a known integral with confidence intervals.
Compare statistical quality, reproducibility and performance.

visual.question: Do two workers accidentally generate the same samples?
visual.interaction: Change launch size while keeping logical sample identities fixed.

practice.task: Implement a Monte Carlo estimator with replayable sample mapping.
practice.success: Estimate agrees with a known answer within justified sampling uncertainty; streams are not accidentally duplicated.
